Natural_Language: This part explains how the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a) and OMB Circular No. A-130 (December 12, 1985) apply to Government contracts. It also references the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552).
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_000_a: Part 24 explains how the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a) applies to Government contracts; P_24_000_b: Part 24 explains how OMB Circular No. A-130 (December 12, 1985) applies to Government contracts; P_24_000_c: Part 24 references the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552)
Validation_Notes: Declarative scope statement. Three conjunctive elements identify the statutory authorities covered by Part 24. No conditional logic required.

Natural_Language: Definitions used in Subpart 24.1 - Protection of Individual Privacy.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_101: Subpart 24.1 definitions consist of seven defined terms: Agency, Individual, Maintain, Operation of a system of records, Personally identifiable information, Record, and System of records on individuals
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for seven definitional entries. All definitions are conjunctively required for interpreting the subpart.

Natural_Language: Agency means any executive department, military department, Government corporation, Government controlled corporation, or other establishment in the executive branch of the Government (including the Executive Office of the President), or any independent regulatory agency.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_101_a_1: Agency includes any executive department; P_24_101_a_2: Agency includes any military department; P_24_101_a_3: Agency includes any Government corporation; P_24_101_a_4: Agency includes any Government controlled corporation; P_24_101_a_5: Agency includes other establishments in the executive branch (including Executive Office of the President); P_24_101_a_6: Agency includes any independent regulatory agency
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive definition. Any one of the listed entity types satisfies the definition of Agency. The 'or' connectors in the original text confirm disjunction.

Natural_Language: Individual means a citizen of the United States or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_101_b_1: Individual is a citizen of the United States; P_24_101_b_2: Individual is an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive definition. Either citizenship or lawful permanent residence satisfies the definition. Mirrors Privacy Act statutory language.

Natural_Language: Maintain means maintain, collect, use, or disseminate.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_101_c_1: Maintain includes maintaining records; P_24_101_c_2: Maintain includes collecting records; P_24_101_c_3: Maintain includes using records; P_24_101_c_4: Maintain includes disseminating records
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive definition. Any one of the four activities constitutes 'maintaining' under this subpart. Broadens the plain meaning of 'maintain' to include collection, use, and dissemination.

Natural_Language: Operation of a system of records means performance of any of the activities associated with maintaining the system of records, including the collection, use, and dissemination of records.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_101_d_1: Operation of a system of records means performance of activities associated with maintaining the system; P_24_101_d_2: Operation includes collection of records; P_24_101_d_3: Operation includes use of records; P_24_101_d_4: Operation includes dissemination of records
Validation_Notes: Hybrid structure. The base definition (performance of activities associated with maintaining) is conjunctive with a non-exhaustive disjunctive list of included activities. Depends on definition of 'Maintain' at P_24_101_c.

Natural_Language: Personally identifiable information means information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, either alone or when combined with other information that is linked or linkable to a specific individual. (See Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular No. A-130, Managing Federal Information as a Strategic Resource).
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_101_e_1: PII is information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity alone; P_24_101_e_2: PII is information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity when combined with other information linked or linkable to a specific individual
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive definition. Information qualifies as PII if it can identify an individual either standing alone OR when combined with other linkable information. References OMB Circular A-130 as external authority.

Natural_Language: Record means any item, collection, or grouping of information about an individual that is maintained by an agency, including, but not limited to, education, financial transactions, medical history, and criminal or employment history, and that contains the individual's name, or the identifying number, symbol, or other identifying particular assigned to the individual, such as a fingerprint or voiceprint or a photograph.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_101_f_1: A record is any item, collection, or grouping of information about an individual; P_24_101_f_2: The record is maintained by an agency; P_24_101_f_3: The record contains the individual's name or an identifying number, symbol, or other identifying particular assigned to the individual
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive definition with three required elements. All three conditions must be met for information to qualify as a 'record.' The non-exhaustive examples (education, financial, medical, etc.) are illustrative, not limiting. Depends on definitions of Agency and Individual.

Natural_Language: System of records on individuals means a group of any records under the control of any agency from which information is retrieved by the name of the individual or by some identifying number, symbol, or other identifying particular assigned to the individual.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_101_g_1: A system of records is a group of records under the control of any agency; P_24_101_g_2: Information is retrieved by the name of the individual; P_24_101_g_3: Information is retrieved by some identifying number, symbol, or other identifying particular assigned to the individual
Validation_Notes: Hybrid structure. Agency control is conjunctively required, while the retrieval method is disjunctive (by name OR by identifying particular). Depends on definitions of Agency, Individual, and Record.

Natural_Language: General requirements for applying Privacy Act requirements to contractors operating systems of records on individuals.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_102: General Privacy Act application requirements consist of four provisions covering agency obligations, criminal penalties, contract-specific requirements, and civil liability
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for four subsections. All provisions apply collectively.

Natural_Language: When an agency hires a contractor to design, develop, or operate a system of records on individuals, the agency must apply the Privacy Act requirements to the contractor and its employees working on the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_102_a_1: An agency hires a contractor to design, develop, or operate a system of records on individuals; P_24_102_a_2: The agency applies Privacy Act requirements to the contractor and its employees working on the contract
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandatory requirement. The trigger condition is hiring a contractor for system of records work. The 'must' modal verb creates a mandatory obligation on the agency once the condition is met. HIGH-RISK flagged due to material implication. Causality direction is clear: contract for SOR work triggers Privacy Act application.

Natural_Language: Both agency staff and contractor employees may face criminal penalties for violating the Privacy Act. When contractors operate a system of records on individuals to accomplish an agency function, the law treats these contractors as agency employees for purposes of the criminal penalties.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_102_b_1: Agency staff may face criminal penalties for violating the Privacy Act; P_24_102_b_2: Contractor employees may face criminal penalties for violating the Privacy Act; P_24_102_b_3: Contractors operate a system of records on individuals to accomplish an agency function; P_24_102_b_4: The law treats contractors as agency employees for purposes of criminal penalties
Validation_Notes: Two-part proposition. First part is conjunctive: both agency staff and contractor employees face criminal penalties. Second part is conditional: when contractors operate SOR for agency function, they are treated as agency employees for penalty purposes. HIGH-RISK flagged for implication component. The 'may face' language indicates potential liability, not certainty of prosecution.

Natural_Language: When a contract specifically calls for designing, developing, or operating a system of records on individuals to accomplish an agency function, the agency must apply Privacy Act requirements to the contractor and its employees working on the contract. The system of records operated under the contract is officially considered to be maintained by the agency for the purposes of the Act.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_102_c_1: A contract specifically calls for designing, developing, or operating a system of records on individuals to accomplish an agency function; P_24_102_c_2: The agency applies Privacy Act requirements to the contractor and its employees working on the contract; P_24_102_c_3: The system of records operated under the contract is considered maintained by the agency for purposes of the Act
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandatory requirement with dual consequent. When the contract specifically requires SOR work for an agency function, two obligations arise conjunctively: (1) Privacy Act applies to contractor/employees, and (2) the SOR is deemed agency-maintained. This is more specific than 24.102(a) by requiring the contract to 'specifically call for' the work and adding the agency-maintenance deeming provision. HIGH-RISK flagged for implication.

Natural_Language: Agencies that, within the limits of their authorities, fail to require contractors to operate systems of records according to the Privacy Act may be civilly liable. If an individual suffers harm due to the contractor's violation of the Act, the agency may be liable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_102_d_1: Agency fails to require contractors to operate systems of records according to the Privacy Act within the limits of its authorities; P_24_102_d_2: Agency may be civilly liable; P_24_102_d_3: An individual suffers harm due to the contractor's violation of the Act; P_24_102_d_4: The agency may be liable for individual harm
Validation_Notes: Two conditional statements joined conjunctively. Both describe potential civil liability scenarios. The 'may be liable' language creates permissive/potential liability, not absolute. First condition: agency failure to require Privacy Act compliance triggers potential liability. Second condition: individual harm from contractor violation triggers potential agency liability. HIGH-RISK flagged for dual material implication.

Natural_Language: Procedures for contracting officers regarding Privacy Act requirements in contracts involving systems of records on individuals.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_103: Privacy Act contracting procedures consist of a review requirement and conditional obligations when SOR work is required
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for two subsections covering CO review and conditional obligations.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must review requirements to determine if they include designing, developing, or operating a system of records on individuals to accomplish an agency function.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_103_a: The contracting officer reviews requirements to determine if they include designing, developing, or operating a system of records on individuals to accomplish an agency function
Justification_Rules: None (atomic proposition; no logical operators applied)
Validation_Notes: Mandatory standalone requirement. The 'must' modal verb creates an unconditional obligation on the contracting officer to perform this review for all requirements. No conditional trigger; this is a universal duty.

Natural_Language: If the contract requires such work, the contracting officer must clearly identify the system and work in the contract work statement and provide the contractor with the agency's Privacy Act implementing rules and regulations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_103_b_cond: The contract requires designing, developing, or operating a system of records on individuals; P_24_103_b: CO fulfills both identification and provision obligations
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandatory requirement with two conjunctive obligations in the consequent. The condition (contract requires SOR work) triggers both sub-obligations. HIGH-RISK flagged for material implication. Causality is clear: determination from 24.103(a) triggers these obligations.

Natural_Language: Clearly identify in the contract work statement both the specific system of records and the design, development, or operation work required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_103_b_1_a: CO identifies in the contract work statement the specific system of records; P_24_103_b_1_b: CO identifies in the contract work statement the design, development, or operation work required
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive requirement. Both the system identification AND the work identification must appear in the contract work statement. The word 'both' explicitly confirms conjunction.

Natural_Language: Provide the contractor with the agency's rules and regulations that implement the Privacy Act.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_103_b_2: CO provides the contractor with the agency's rules and regulations implementing the Privacy Act
Justification_Rules: None (atomic proposition; no logical operators applied)
Validation_Notes: Mandatory standalone requirement under the conditional parent 24.103(b). Atomic proposition with no internal logical structure.

Natural_Language: When a contract requires designing, developing, or operating a system of records on individuals to accomplish an agency function, the contracting officer must include the following clauses in solicitations and contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_104_cond: A contract requires designing, developing, or operating a system of records on individuals to accomplish an agency function; P_24_104: CO includes required clauses in solicitations and contracts
Validation_Notes: Conditional clause insertion requirement. SOR contract work triggers mandatory inclusion of both specified clauses. Parent proposition with two child clause requirements. HIGH-RISK flagged for material implication.

Natural_Language: The clause at 52.224-1, Privacy Act Notification.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_104_a: CO includes the clause at 52.224-1, Privacy Act Notification, in solicitations and contracts
Justification_Rules: None (atomic proposition; no logical operators applied)
Validation_Notes: Clause prescription. References FAR 52.224-1 as external dependency (Part 52). Mandatory under the conditional trigger of P_24_104.

Natural_Language: The clause at 52.224-2, Privacy Act.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_104_b: CO includes the clause at 52.224-2, Privacy Act, in solicitations and contracts
Justification_Rules: None (atomic proposition; no logical operators applied)
Validation_Notes: Clause prescription. References FAR 52.224-2 as external dependency (Part 52). Mandatory under the conditional trigger of P_24_104.

Natural_Language: The Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552) requires that information be made available to the public through three methods.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_201: FOIA requires information availability through three specified methods
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. All three methods are conjunctively required under FOIA. The statute mandates all three availability methods, not a choice among them.

Natural_Language: Publication in the Federal Register.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_201_a: Information is made available to the public through publication in the Federal Register
Justification_Rules: None (atomic proposition; no logical operators applied)
Validation_Notes: First FOIA availability method. Atomic proposition, no internal logical structure.

Natural_Language: Access to read and copy records at convenient locations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_201_b: Information is made available through access to read and copy records at convenient locations
Justification_Rules: None (atomic proposition; no logical operators applied)
Validation_Notes: Second FOIA availability method. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: Providing a copy of a reasonably described record upon request.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_201_c: Information is made available through providing a copy of a reasonably described record upon request
Justification_Rules: None (atomic proposition; no logical operators applied)
Validation_Notes: Third FOIA availability method. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: FOIA disclosure prohibitions applicable to agencies regarding proposals, information obtained under Part 15, and dispute resolution communications.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_202: FOIA prohibitions consist of three categories of protected information
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for three prohibition subsections. All prohibitions apply conjunctively.

Natural_Language: An agency must not disclose under the Freedom of Information Act any proposal submitted in response to solicitation for competitive proposals. This prohibition does not apply to a proposal, or any part of a proposal, that is included or incorporated by reference in a contract between the Government and the contractor that submitted the proposal. (See 10 U.S.C. 3309 and 41 U.S.C. 4702.)
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_202_a_1: Agency does not disclose under FOIA any proposal submitted in response to solicitation for competitive proposals; P_24_202_a_2: The proposal or part thereof is included or incorporated by reference in a contract between the Government and the submitting contractor; P_24_202_a_3: The prohibition at P_24_202_a_1 does not apply
Justification_Rules: Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with exception. Base rule prohibits disclosure of competitive proposals. Exception: when proposal content is incorporated into the resulting contract, the prohibition is lifted. 'Must not' creates mandatory negative obligation. The exception uses material implication: if proposal is in the contract, then prohibition does not apply. References 10 U.S.C. 3309 and 41 U.S.C. 4702 as statutory authorities. HIGH-RISK flagged for implication in the exception clause.

Natural_Language: An agency must not disclose outside the Government any information obtained under part 15 that is exempt from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act. (See 10 U.S.C. 3705(c)(3) and 41 U.S.C. 3505(b)(3).)
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_202_b_1: Information is obtained under Part 15; P_24_202_b_2: Information is exempt from disclosure under FOIA; P_24_202_b_3: Agency does not disclose the information outside the Government
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional prohibition. Two conjunctive conditions (obtained under Part 15 AND FOIA-exempt) trigger the non-disclosure obligation. 'Must not' is mandatory negative. External dependency on Part 15 (Contracting by Negotiation). References 10 U.S.C. 3705(c)(3) and 41 U.S.C. 3505(b)(3). HIGH-RISK flagged for material implication.

Natural_Language: A dispute resolution communication between a neutral person and a party to alternative dispute resolution proceedings that is protected under 5 U.S.C. 574(j) is exempt from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552(b)(3)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_202_c_1: A dispute resolution communication occurs between a neutral person and a party to ADR proceedings; P_24_202_c_2: The communication is protected under 5 U.S.C. 574(j); P_24_202_c_3: The communication is exempt from disclosure under FOIA (5 U.S.C. 552(b)(3))
Validation_Notes: Conditional exemption. Two conjunctive conditions (ADR communication between neutral and party AND protected under 5 U.S.C. 574(j)) trigger FOIA exemption. Declarative 'is exempt' language. References two statutory provisions. HIGH-RISK flagged for material implication.

Natural_Language: FOIA policy requirements for agency records disclosure, exemptions, and contracting officer guidance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_203: FOIA policy consists of three provisions covering agency disclosure requirements, common exemptions, and CO compliance guidance
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for three policy subsections.

Natural_Language: The Freedom of Information Act specifies how agencies must make their records available upon public request, sets strict time standards for agency responses, and exempts certain records from public disclosure. Each agency's implementation of these requirements appears in its respective title of the Code of Federal Regulations and is referenced in subpart 24.2 of its implementing acquisition regulations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_203_a_1: FOIA specifies how agencies must make records available upon public request; P_24_203_a_2: FOIA sets strict time standards for agency responses; P_24_203_a_3: FOIA exempts certain records from public disclosure; P_24_203_a_4: Each agency's FOIA implementation appears in its respective CFR title and is referenced in subpart 24.2 of its implementing acquisition regulations
Validation_Notes: Declarative policy statement with four conjunctive elements describing FOIA's scope and agency implementation requirements. No conditional logic. Primarily informational.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers may receive requests for records that may be exempt from mandatory public disclosure. The most common exemptions are for trade secrets and confidential commercial or financial information (5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4)). Other exemptions include certain interagency or intra-agency memoranda, classified information, internal personnel rules, personal and medical information about individuals, and law enforcement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_203_b_1: Contracting officers may receive requests for records that may be exempt from mandatory public disclosure; P_24_203_b_2: The most common exemptions are for trade secrets and confidential commercial or financial information under 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4); P_24_203_b_3: Other exemptions include interagency/intra-agency memoranda, classified information, internal personnel rules, personal and medical information, and law enforcement
Validation_Notes: Informational policy statement. Describes the types of FOIA exemption requests COs may encounter. No mandatory obligation created; uses 'may receive' (descriptive). The exemption categories are informational, not exhaustive.

Natural_Language: Since these requests often involve complex issues requiring in-depth knowledge of court rulings and policy guidance, contracting officers must comply with their agency's implementing regulations. Contracting officers should obtain necessary guidance from agency officials responsible for Freedom of Information Act compliance. For additional assistance, authorized agency officials may contact the Department of Justice, Office of Information and Privacy.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_203_c_1: FOIA requests involve complex issues requiring in-depth knowledge of court rulings and policy guidance; P_24_203_c_2: Contracting officers comply with their agency's FOIA implementing regulations; P_24_203_c_3: Contracting officers obtain necessary guidance from agency FOIA officials; P_24_203_c_4: Authorized agency officials may contact DOJ Office of Information and Privacy for additional assistance
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Mixed-obligation provision. First sentence: 'must comply' is mandatory, triggered by the complexity rationale (conditional). Second sentence: 'should obtain' is advisory (non-binding recommendation, expressed as atomic). Third sentence: 'may contact' is permissive (tautology representing discretion). HIGH-RISK flagged for material implication in the mandatory component. Advisory 'should' noted per modal verb mapping.

Natural_Language: [Reserved]
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_301: Section reserved; no current regulatory content
Validation_Notes: Reserved section. No substantive regulatory content. Placeholder maintained for structural completeness.

Natural_Language: Privacy training contract clause requirements for solicitations and contracts involving contractor access to systems of records or personally identifiable information.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_302: Privacy training clause requirements consist of a mandatory clause insertion provision and an alternate clause provision
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for two subsections covering mandatory clause insertion and alternate clause usage.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must insert the clause at FAR 52.224-3, Privacy Training, in solicitations and contracts when, on behalf of the agency, contractor employees will have access to a system of records; create, collect, use, process, store, maintain, disseminate, disclose, dispose, or otherwise handle personally identifiable information; or design, develop, maintain, or operate a system of records.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_302_a_1: Contractor employees will have access to a system of records on behalf of the agency; P_24_302_a_2: Contractor employees will create, collect, use, process, store, maintain, disseminate, disclose, dispose, or otherwise handle PII on behalf of the agency; P_24_302_a_3: Contractor employees will design, develop, maintain, or operate a system of records on behalf of the agency; P_24_302_a_4: CO inserts the clause at FAR 52.224-3, Privacy Training, in solicitations and contracts
Validation_Notes: Conditional clause insertion requirement. Any one of three disjunctive triggers (SOR access, PII handling, or SOR design/development/maintenance/operation) mandates clause insertion. The 'must' modal verb creates mandatory obligation. The 'or' connecting the three conditions confirms disjunction. External dependency on FAR 52.224-3 (Part 52). HIGH-RISK flagged for material implication.

Natural_Language: Have access to a system of records.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_302_a_1: Contractor employees will have access to a system of records on behalf of the agency
Justification_Rules: None (atomic proposition; no logical operators applied)
Validation_Notes: First disjunctive trigger for Privacy Training clause insertion. Atomic proposition representing SOR access condition.

Natural_Language: Create, collect, use, process, store, maintain, disseminate, disclose, dispose, or otherwise handle personally identifiable information.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_302_a_2: Contractor employees will create, collect, use, process, store, maintain, disseminate, disclose, dispose, or otherwise handle PII on behalf of the agency
Justification_Rules: None (atomic proposition; no logical operators applied)
Validation_Notes: Second disjunctive trigger for Privacy Training clause insertion. The enumerated activities (create, collect, use, etc.) are themselves disjunctive -- any one activity involving PII triggers this condition. Treated as atomic because the enumeration defines a single concept: PII handling.

Natural_Language: Design, develop, maintain, or operate a system of records.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_302_a_3: Contractor employees will design, develop, maintain, or operate a system of records on behalf of the agency
Justification_Rules: None (atomic proposition; no logical operators applied)
Validation_Notes: Third disjunctive trigger for Privacy Training clause insertion. Activities are disjunctive (any one triggers the condition). Treated as atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: When an agency specifies that only its agency-provided training is acceptable, use the clause with its Alternate I.
Atomic_Propositions: P_24_302_b_1: An agency specifies that only its agency-provided training is acceptable; P_24_302_b_2: CO uses the clause at FAR 52.224-3 with its Alternate I
Validation_Notes: Conditional clause modification requirement. When the agency restricts acceptable training to its own, the Alternate I version must be used. Implicit mandatory obligation (imperative 'use'). HIGH-RISK flagged for material implication. Depends on P_24_302_a being triggered first.
